title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is page 69 of the third version of Grothendieck's axiomatic, combinatorial 'Analysis situs' (June 1986). The data are a set M of 'strata' (elementary cells), several relations on M (≤, ≪, and a compatibility relation written ≬), a class 𝓕 of 'figures', and 'supports' Σ of parts A ⊂ M. On p.68 he handles the 'quasi-set-theoretic' case. There a set ℙ of 'points' exists, pairwise incompatible, and supports identify with the power set 𝔓(ℙ), compatibly with complementation. In that case supp A = ⋃_{F∈A} comb_∧(F).

Opening remark of p.69 (25 June). Outside the quasi-set-theoretic case, he suspects that the notion of support as presented is 'caduque' (obsolete). One should speak of the support of A ⊂ M only when:
- the X ∈ A are mutually compatible, or
- they admit, pairwise, unions that are mutually compatible.
This is a methodological retreat: the support/union operations should be partial, defined only on coherent families, not total Boolean operations.

Typical example: strata of an ordered set I (e.g. an 'ordered segment').
- M = M0 ⊔ M1.
- M0 = I = Drap_0(I): the 0-strata (points).
- M1 = Drap_1(I): the 1-strata, i.e. the closed subsegments X = I_{a≤·≤b} with a < b. The endpoints a, b are uniquely determined (origin and extremity), and ∂X := {a, b}.

Three relations on M:
1. X ≤ Y ⇔ X = Y, or (X ∈ M0, Y ∈ M1, X ∈ ∂Y). This is the face/incidence relation: the closure order of a 1-dimensional cell complex.
2. X ≪ Y ⇔ X ⊂ Y as subsets of I. This is containment of underlying point sets, so an interior point or a subsegment is ≪ a segment without being a face of it.
3. X ≬ Y (compatibility) holds iff exactly one of three mutually exclusive cases occurs:
   (a) X = Y;
   (b) X ∈ ∂Y or Y ∈ ∂X, i.e. a point that is an endpoint of a segment;
   (c) ∂X ∪ ∂Y is totally ordered and X ∩ Y is empty or a single point. Concretely: either (α) X = [a,b], Y = [c,d] with a ≤ b < c ≤ d (disjoint), or (β) X = [a,b], Y = [b,c] with a < b < c (abutting), or the same with X and Y swapped.
   The marginal figures illustrate (b), and (c) in its disjoint and adjacent forms.

Compatible families are exactly the cells that can coexist in a 'subdivided' 1-dimensional figure. Next page: figures = finite parts F ⊂ M that are closed under ≤ (contain the endpoints of their segments) and pairwise compatible. These are finite 1-dimensional cell complexes 'drawn' in I: finitely many points and non-overlapping closed segments.

Final NB: all axioms of his system hold except Ax 1 (divisibility). Ax 1 holds iff every open interval ]a,b[ (a < b) is nonempty, i.e. iff I is densely ordered.

Purpose. To test the abstract axioms on the simplest non-set-theoretic model: the 'tame' (modérée) combinatorics of the ordered line. This is the 1-dimensional germ of his programme of 'topologie modérée' (Esquisse d'un programme §5). The constructible subsets of I are finite unions of points and intervals, as in o-minimal geometry. Here supports cannot be a Boolean algebra of subsets of a point set without partiality constraints.
errors: If 'ensemble ordonné' allows a partial order, condition (c) makes two distinct incomparable points (∂X ∪ ∂Y = {x,y} not totally ordered) incompatible. Two incomparable segments would likewise be incompatible. For figures in a poset this seems unintended, or at least unexplained. Presumably I is meant to be totally ordered ('segment ordonné'), in which case the total-order clause is vacuous.

In (c)(α) the inequality a ≤ b < c ≤ d is written to cover degenerate (point) cases. With a < b required for segments, the case analysis for point-versus-segment (point outside the segment) is only implicit. A point lying strictly inside a segment is correctly excluded, but this is not stated.

The opening criterion ('mutually compatible, or pairwise admitting unions that are mutually compatible') is stated loosely and not made precise. The page itself calls the support notion possibly 'caduque' without a replacement definition.

ideas.what: Supports/unions should be defined only on mutually compatible (coherent) families of strata, not as total Boolean operations, outside the quasi-set-theoretic case
ideas.modern_name: partial lattice operations on consistent subsets (coherence spaces / Scott domains: joins exist for bounded or consistent sets)

ideas.what: Strata of an ordered set: points and closed subsegments, with face relation ≤, inclusion ≪, boundary ∂X = {a,b}
ideas.modern_name: face poset of a 1-dimensional cell decomposition of an ordered line; Drap_k as k-flags of I
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (cell complexes; o-minimal cell decomposition: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn 1984-86)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5 (1984); detailed combinatorics unpublished

ideas.what: Compatibility relation ≬ (equal, endpoint-incidence, or disjoint/abutting); figures = finite ≤-closed pairwise compatible sets
ideas.modern_name: finite subcomplexes / finite cliques of a coherence relation closed under faces

ideas.what: Divisibility axiom (Ax 1) holds iff the order is dense

missed.claim: Grothendieck's axiomatics replace Boolean support operations by operations defined only on families of mutually compatible cells, using a reflexive symmetric compatibility relation whose finite down-closed cliques are the 'figures'. This is formally very close to coherence spaces and Scott-style consistency, developed at the same moment in logic. The connection between tame-topology combinatorics and coherence-space structure is not drawn in the literature.
missed.quote: qu'il ne faudrait parler de support d'une partie A de M ... que quand les X ∈ A sont mutuellement compatibles
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests viewing tame/o-minimal cell structures as coherence-space-like objects. This could be relevant for formal and synthetic approaches to tame topology. The link is modest and suggestive only.

missed.claim: The abstract theory of 'supports' for non-quasi-set-theoretic stratified structures is flagged as possibly obsolete and left without a replacement definition.
missed.quote: je suspecte que la notion de support, telle qu'elle est présentée ici, est caduque
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an open design point in Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic tame topology. It is of historical interest; it is unlikely to contain a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The worked example is the elementary combinatorics of points and segments on an ordered line, with a dense-order remark. Its interest is mainly as documentation of Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic tame topology and his shift toward partial, compatibility-restricted operations. There is no new result.
transcription_corrections: Opening sentence reads roughly: '... que quand les X ∈ A sont mutuellement compatibles, ou dont, deux à deux, ils admettent des unions, mutuellement compatibles. Voici un exemple typique.' The transcription's duplicated 'des unions, de deux à deux' is garbled.
In the example title, 'segment' is struck out and replaced by 'ens.' ('Strates associées à un ens. ordonné I'), as the transcription indicates; M0 = Drap_0(I) confirmed.
The parenthetical in case (b) is better read as '(cas où Y, supp. X, est dans M1)', i.e. the segment is the one in M1. It is not 'Y supp. X est dans M1' as a single phrase.

Top-right marginalia near the ≬ definition contain crossed-out notation 'X ⊲ Y' / 'X ⊀ Y' that the transcription omits. These look like abandoned symbols for the relations, but the reading is uncertain.
Bottom NB: 'Ax 1 (divisibilité) satisfait ssi les intervalles ]a,b[ sont ≠ ∅ (a<b)' is confirmed.
